articles.title: Grammar Games at Home: Jeopardy
articles.description: With so many people stuck at home, Everyday Grammar will be offering ideas for games that you can play with your family or housemates to practice your English. Today's game is Jeopardy.
articles.license: VOA Learning English 公有领域文本
articles.credit: Alice Bryant wrote this story for Learning English. George Grow was the editor.

articles.title: Wilbur and Orville Wright: The First Airplane
articles.description: Wilbur and Orville Wright quietly developed a powered flying machine that proved heavier-than-air flight was possible more than 120 years ago.
articles.license: VOA Learning English 公有领域文本
articles.credit: Marilyn Rice Christiano wrote this story for VOA Learning English. John Russell adapted it.

articles.title: Lincoln's Cottage: a Country House for the President
articles.description: About five kilometers from the White House in Washington, DC lies an historic building closely linked to the life of one of America’s most famous presidents: Abraham Lincoln. The building, known as President Lincoln's Cottage, is where he spent about one-fourth of his presidency.
articles.license: VOA Learning English 公有领域文本
articles.credit: Nancy Steinbach wrote this story for VOA Learning English. John Russell adapted it.

articles.title: Common Adverbs in Conversation: Amplifiers, Downtoners
articles.description: In this Everyday Grammar program, we examine some of the most important adverbs that you will hear in everyday speech. There is even a special name for them. They are called amplifiers and downtoners.
articles.license: VOA Learning English 公有领域文本
articles.credit: John Russell wrote this story for Learning English. George Grow was the editor.

articles.title: Philadelphia: a City Famous for its History
articles.description: Philadelphia is also called "the city of brotherly love." Established by William Penn in the 1680s, the city was important to the American independence movement and was for a time the United States capital.
articles.license: VOA Learning English 公有领域文本
articles.credit: Nancy Steinbach wrote this story for VOA Learning English. John Russell adapted it.

articles.title: Adverb and Adjective Choices in Conversation
articles.description: In today's Everyday Grammar, we will study how conversational grammar differs from written and formal grammatical structures. Americans often use adjective forms in place of adverbs. Americans also may use an adverb but choose not to say an –ly ending.
articles.license: VOA Learning English 公有领域文本
articles.credit: John Russell wrote this story for Learning English. Caty Weaver was the editor.

articles.title: Skyscrapers, Made in America
articles.description: Tall buildings were limited before the 1880s because of construction materials and safety. Two developments helped them to grow – safer elevators and steel.
articles.license: VOA Learning English 公有领域文本
articles.credit: Jerilyn Watson reported this story for VOA Learning English. Jill Robbins adapted it for VOA Learning English with additional materials.

articles.title: Academic Writing: Common Sentence Patterns, Part Four
articles.description: English has many patterns. Learning and mastering these patterns can help you improve your writing and speaking skills. Today's common pattern is the transitive verb pattern. There are several types of transitive verbs, but they all have one thing in common: a direct object.

articles.credit: John Russell wrote this story for Learning English. George Grow was the editor.

articles.title: Academic Writing: Common Sentence Patterns, Part Two
articles.description: In this week's report, we are going to explore one pattern that is commonly used in academic writing. Academic writers often use it to judge an idea. The structure we are exploring starts with a noun followed by a "that clause."
articles.license: VOA Learning English 公有领域文本

articles.title: Academic Writing: Common Sentence Patterns, Part One
articles.description: Today on Everyday Grammar, we explore two grammatical structures that you will see often in academic writing. These structures are used to evaluate ideas and evaluate actions. articles.license: VOA Learning English 公有领域文本
articles.credit: John Russell wrote this story for Learning English. George Grow was the editor.

articles.title: Studying Sentence Patterns to Improve Your Writing, Part Two
articles.description: This week, we give you more information about a common sentence pattern in English: the linking verb pattern. Learning how to use linking verb patterns will help you improve your writing. You can think about creative ways to use them, or you can learn to recognize when you use them too often.
articles.license: VOA Learning English 公有领域文本
articles.credit: John Russell wrote this story for Learning English. Kelly J. Kelly was the editor.
